proof:
Notation: E := Amb n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, H := μHE[n], H⌞X := H.restrict X, Φ_#ν := Measure.map Φ ν, κ := ((1 − δ)⁻¹)ⁿ ∈ ℝ and κ̂ := ENNReal.ofReal κ ∈ [0, ∞].
1. Bi-Lipschitz bounds. Let p, q ∈ A and put e := Φ p − Φ q − (p − q), so ‖e‖ ≤ δ‖p − q‖ by hypothesis.
   - Upper bound: ‖Φ p − Φ q‖ = ‖e + (p − q)‖ ≤ ‖e‖ + ‖p − q‖ ≤ (1 + δ)‖p − q‖.
   - Lower bound: ‖p − q‖ = ‖(Φ p − Φ q) − e‖ ≤ ‖Φ p − Φ q‖ + δ‖p − q‖, i.e. (1 − δ)‖p − q‖ ≤ ‖Φ p − Φ q‖.
   Note that 1 − δ > 0 and 1 + δ ≥ 1 > 0.
2. Measurability. By step 1, Φ is (1 + δ)-Lipschitz on A, i.e. LipschitzOnWith (Real.toNNReal (1 + δ)) Φ A (via LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul). Hence Φ is continuous on A. Since A is measurable, Φ is a.e.-measurable for H⌞A (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable).
3. A Lipschitz left inverse.
   - Φ is injective on A: if p, q ∈ A and Φ p = Φ q, step 1 gives (1 − δ)‖p − q‖ ≤ 0, so p = q because 1 − δ > 0.
   - Let Ψ := Function.invFunOn Φ A. Then Ψ(Φ p) = p for all p ∈ A (Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn).
   - Let a = Φ p and b = Φ q with p, q ∈ A. By step 1, ‖Ψ a − Ψ b‖ = ‖p − q‖ ≤ (1 − δ)⁻¹‖Φ p − Φ q‖ = (1 − δ)⁻¹‖a − b‖. So Ψ is (1 − δ)⁻¹-Lipschitz on Φ(A).
4. Constants. (1 + δ)(1 − δ) = 1 − δ² ≤ 1 and 1 − δ > 0, so 1 + δ ≤ (1 − δ)⁻¹. Since 1 + δ ≥ 0, this gives (1 + δ)ⁿ ≤ κ (pow_le_pow_left₀). In [0, ∞]:
   - (Real.toNNReal (1 + δ))ⁿ = ENNReal.ofReal((1 + δ)ⁿ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal κ = κ̂ (ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal);
   - (Real.toNNReal ((1 − δ)⁻¹))ⁿ = ENNReal.ofReal(((1 − δ)⁻¹)ⁿ) = κ̂.
5. Lipschitz image bound (Simon, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.8(i); it needs no measurability of the set). If a map f is c-Lipschitz on a set T ⊆ E (c ∈ ℝ≥0), then H(f(T)) ≤ cⁿ H(T). This is Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn n. Being Lipschitz on a set passes to its subsets (LipschitzOnWith.mono).
6. Evaluation on measurable sets. Let S ⊆ E be measurable.
   - By Measure.map_apply_of_aemeasurable (using step 2), Φ_#(H⌞A)(S) = (H⌞A)(Φ⁻¹(S)).
   - By Measure.restrict_apply', which only needs A measurable (Φ⁻¹(S) need not be measurable), (H⌞A)(Φ⁻¹(S)) = H(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A).
   - By Measure.restrict_apply (S measurable), (H⌞Φ(A))(S) = H(S ∩ Φ(A)).
   - S ∩ Φ(A) = Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A) (Set.image_preimage_inter).
   - For every measure ν, (κ̂ · ν)(S) = κ̂ · ν(S) (Measure.smul_apply).
7. First inequality. Φ is (1 + δ)-Lipschitz on Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A ⊆ A. By steps 6, 5 and 4:
   (H⌞Φ(A))(S) = H(Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A)) ≤ (Real.toNNReal (1 + δ))ⁿ · H(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A) ≤ κ̂ · H(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A) = (κ̂ · Φ_#(H⌞A))(S).
8. Second inequality. Ψ ∘ Φ = id on Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A ⊆ A, so Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A = Ψ(Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A)) (Set.LeftInvOn.image_image). Also Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A) ⊆ Φ(A), where Ψ is (1 − δ)⁻¹-Lipschitz by step 3. By steps 6, 5 and 4:
   Φ_#(H⌞A)(S) = H(Ψ(Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A))) ≤ (Real.toNNReal ((1 − δ)⁻¹))ⁿ · H(Φ(Φ⁻¹(S) ∩ A)) = κ̂ · H(S ∩ Φ(A)) = (κ̂ · H⌞Φ(A))(S).
9. Conclusion. For measures, μ ≤ ν holds iff μ(S) ≤ ν(S) for every measurable S (Measure.le_iff). Steps 7 and 8 therefore give H⌞Φ(A) ≤ κ̂ · Φ_#(H⌞A) and Φ_#(H⌞A) ≤ κ̂ · H⌞Φ(A). This is the claimed conjunction.

(1 + δ)ⁿ ≤ κ = ((1 − δ)⁻¹)ⁿ because (1 + δ)(1 − δ) ≤ 1; translate to ENNReal.ofReal
for measurable S: Φ_#(H⌞A)(S) = H(Φ⁻¹S ∩ A) and H⌞Φ(A)(S) = H(S ∩ Φ(A)) = H(Φ(Φ⁻¹S ∩ A))
